classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish interest on the original principal from interest on the changing balance, then translate the completed tables into straight-line and curved graphs on supplied labelled axes. These are routine linked procedures taught in context.

content.prompt: An amount of $\$10\,000$ is to be invested at 8.5% per annum for 5 years. For compound interest, interest is compounded annually. Give monetary entries to 2 decimal places where needed, retaining unrounded values in calculations.

inlines.text: Complete the table if invested as
Simple interest uses the original principal each year. Interest = original principal × 8.5%. Display amounts to cents and retain unrounded values in intermediate calculations.
Complete the table if invested as
Each ending balance becomes the next starting balance. Interest = starting balance × 8.5%. Display amounts to cents and retain unrounded values in intermediate calculations.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Draw the two graphs on the same axes to show how the value of the investment changes for each option over the 5 years.

spec.description: Shared portrait coordinate grid with arrowed axes, unlabelled zero, half-year vertical grid lines, annual labelled ticks and $1000 horizontal intervals. Extend the top from $15000 to $16000 so both five-year values fit.
spec.mathematics: Horizontal coordinate is years, 0 to 5. Vertical TikZ coordinate is thousands of dollars, 0 to 16; numeric labels express dollar values.
spec.answerVisibility: Blank question graph: no investment curves or answer points.

answer.short: Both graphs start at $(0,10\,000)$. Simple interest is a straight line ending at $(5,14\,250)$; compound interest is an increasing exponential curve ending at $(5,15\,036.57)$.
answer.worked: Plot each table's ending balance at its year, including the initial point $(0,10\,000)$ for both options. Join the simple-interest points with a straight line and the compound-interest points with a smooth increasing curve. Simple-interest points: $(1,10\,850)$, $(2,11\,700)$, $(3,12\,550)$, $(4,13\,400)$, $(5,14\,250)$. Compound-interest points: $(1,10\,850)$, $(2,11\,772.25)$, $(3,12\,772.89)$, $(4,13\,858.59)$, $(5,15\,036.57)$.

spec.description: Self-contained completed graph with both series on the corrected question coordinate grid, annual points and distinct matching legends. Smooth compound curve follows the page 3 teaching convention.
spec.mathematics: Simple value in dollars is 10000+850t. Compound curve in dollars is 10000(1.085)^t for 0<=t<=5; annual points use unrounded table values. TikZ vertical units are thousands of dollars.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only: both curves, annual points and series legends are supplied.
